patch.value: Exact-tag npm recovery must stabilize public package access before verification

A workflow_dispatch rerun for an immutable published tag can observe stale anonymous public metadata, skip npm access recovery, pass isolated verification, and leave the package private seconds later. Harden exact-tag recovery so public access is explicitly restored before anonymous package/version probes and remains verified without republishing or moving the tag.

workflow_dispatch recovery explicitly sets @unbrained/pm-cli public before anonymous probes; existing immutable versions are never republished or retagged; executable workflow contracts cover recovery ordering and failure behavior; the existing v2026.7.30 tag is recovered and independently verifies through npm, npx, and bunx
An exact-tag recovery explicitly restores the public access invariant before probing the immutable version, skips republishing an existing version, and verifies npm, npx, and bunx anonymously.

Release run 30591621395 saw v2026.7.30 publicly through its clean caches and skipped publication, but independent anonymous metadata returned E404 26 seconds later and npm access status reported private.

value.text: Second Greptile loop found a valid dispatch race: checking out the default-branch name could advance after dispatch. Fixed by pinning workflow_dispatch checkout to github.sha and adding an early fail-closed guard that requires GITHUB_REF_NAME to equal the repository default branch. This simultaneously prevents non-main dispatch and preserves exact dispatch-time source. Focused contracts 30/30, typecheck, and docs/skills pass.
